title: Existence of minimal finite graded free presentations
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with standard total-degree grading [def-sc-p1-standard], and set $I=(x_0,x_1)$. Let $N$ be an $S$-module internally graded by $\mathbf Z$ with $S_nN_j\subseteq N_{n+j}$, and suppose a finite set of homogeneous elements spans $N$. Then there are a finite graded free $S$-module $F$ with homogeneous basis $e_i$ indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, degrees $d_i\in\mathbf Z$, and a degree-zero surjective $S$-linear map $q:F\to N$ such that $q^{-1}(IN)\subseteq IF$. These are the data of a minimal graded presentation [def-sc-p1-minimal-graded-presentation], with its target fixed to $N$ and its given grading. No Tor hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Restrict scalars from S=k[x_0,x_1] to k via constant polynomials. In Q=N/IN, every polynomial acts by its constant coefficient. Thus the finite homogeneous generating set gives a finite k-spanning set of Q. Extract a k-basis from these images and retain the homogeneous lifts n_i with their integer degrees d_i. This uses finite-dimensional linear algebra, and also covers the empty basis when Q=0.

Take F=Fin r → S. Its degree-j subgroup consists of tuples whose ith coefficient is homogeneous of degree j-d_i, or zero when j-d_i<0. Coordinatewise homogeneous polynomial decomposition, with degrees translated by d_i, gives an internal direct sum: all translated supports have finite union, and uniqueness follows coordinatewise. Homogeneous multiplication adds degrees. The standard basis e_i lies in degree d_i. Define q(a)=sum_i a_i n_i; the given scalar compatibility proves that q preserves degrees.

Apply [lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation] to the lifted homogeneous basis to see that q is surjective. If q(a) is in IN, independence of the basis modulo I forces every constant coefficient of a_i to be zero. The kernel of constant coefficient is the ideal I=(x_0,x_1), so every a_i lies in I. Expanding a in the finite standard basis gives a in IF, which is minimality. The empty-basis case gives N=0 by the same graded Nakayama theorem.
